transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-09-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (Redwood AE), Devon Shah (Redwood SE), Lina Ortega (Redwood Product), Priya Singh (Willowbrook Head of Data Platforms), Tom Reynolds (Willowbrook CTO), Sara Milton (Willowbrook Compliance), Jordan Lee (Willowbrook SRE), Alex Park (Willowbrook PM)

Summary:
Quick demo and playbook for configuring request storage, PII redaction, and log slimming in Redwood Console and the API. Customer wants to understand tradeoffs for retaining request payloads vs ephemeral, encryption/KMS options, and how Optimize suggests batching/quantization while preserving privacy. Action items and pilot signup at end.

Topics covered:
- Console toggles: request storage on/off, ephemeral mode, tokenized retention levels
- API flags: storeRequests=true/false, redactionProfiles, pii_detect=true
- KMS and HSM encryption at rest, key rotation notes
- RBAC + SSO and audit logs for compliance team
- Optimize recommendations and cost impact for batching + quantization
- Perf baseline and canary policies for private deployments

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, auto transcript quality medium - occasional mis-words):

[00:00] Elena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, good to see the Willowbrook crew. We got about 55 minutes, we'll run through the console playbook for privacy slimming and the API flags, and then leave time for questions. Devon's going to drive the demo.

[00:27] Tom Reynolds: Thanks Elena, we've got Sara and Jordan here cause compliance and ops want to vet this. High-level ask: we want to host student support chat logs but minimize PII retention and still have the telemetry to troubleshoot. So how granular can we get?

[00:42] Devon Shah: Great, that is exactly the use case we built controls for. Quick caveat: I'm going to share my screen with the Console. Also we'll reference the API flags so you can automate this in your pipeline.

[01:10] Priya Singh: Perfect. Also timeline: we need to validate in two weeks and decide end of month for pilot scale.

[01:25] Devon Shah: Understood. Ok pull up Console home... (screen noise) ...Alright, first section is Request Storage. You can choose three modes: Persist, Ephemeral, and Selective. Persist keeps request and response payloads for X days, Ephemeral stores only for the length of the KV session and then drops after TTL, Selective lets you apply redaction profiles per route.

[02:03] Sara Milton: When you say Ephemeral - is that zero retention in logs? Like will anything hit S3 or our logging plane?

[02:15] Devon Shah: Good question. Ephemeral mode avoids long-term object storage. We still log minimal telemetry for billing and rate-limiting—those are sanitized and token-count only. No full prompt or response payload is written to object storage when ephemeral is enabled. However, if you enable debug snapshot for a route it will temporarily capture a snapshot for up to 1 hour for troubleshooting.

[02:42] Jordan Lee: And those snapshots are encrypted with customer KMS? We need BYOK possibility.

[02:50] Lina Ortega: Yes, we support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault). Snapshots and persisted request storage can be configured to use your KMS keys. We also have optional HSM-backed keys for enterprise.

[03:12] Tom Reynolds: Is rotation automated or manual?

[03:18] Devon Shah: Rotation is customer-controlled. You can trigger key rotation from Console or via API call. We keep metadata to locate historical objects encrypted with prior keys, but access is gated and logged.

[03:36] Priya Singh: OK. Show me the redaction profiles.

[03:42] Devon Shah: Sure. Under Privacy -> Redaction profiles, you can create rules that run before storage. We have prebuilt profiles: pii_basic, pii_strict, and pii_custom. pii_basic will scrub obvious names, SSNs, dob patterns; strict will also remove free-form identifiers and attempt entity-based redaction; custom lets you upload regex lists or a sample dataset for model-assisted training.

[04:12] Priya Singh: Model-assisted? We're nervous about ML changing outputs. How deterministic is that?

[04:20] Devon Shah: It's deterministic in the pipeline sense - the redaction step produces a masked output and the masked tokens and confidence scores are stored in audit logs. You can tune sensitivity. We also support a "review queue" so anything flagged above a threshold gets a compliance review job rather than automatic drop.

[04:42] Sara Milton: Do you capture the original text anywhere for audits?

[04:50] Devon Shah: Only if you opt-in to store originals for X days and with BYOK encryption. Otherwise originals are not persisted. Audit logs contain metadata and a redaction diff, not full original.

[05:08] Elena Park: Quick point - you can also set per-route policies via API. For instance, support-chat route -> pii_strict + ephemeral true. Billing-route -> persist for 30 days.

[05:25] Priya Singh: Show me the API example for that.

[05:30] Devon Shah: Sure. Example curl (paraphrased):
POST /v1/requests
Headers: Authorization: Bearer <token>
Body: {"model":"rw-large","input":"...","storeRequests":false,"redactionProfile":"pii_strict","debugSnapshot":false}
(we also support route-based policies via the policies API so you don't need to send flags every call)

[06:02] Jordan Lee: If we set storeRequests=false, how do we do troubleshooting when a customer reports a bad reply?

[06:12] Devon Shah: Two approaches: (1) You can enable debugSnapshot for short windows tied to a trace-id which will create a signed, time-limited snapshot and only be accessible by people with RBAC permission. (2) Use prefix-based KV caching logs - we keep request hash and token counts so you can retrieve the conversational context if you have a reference id, if you allowed ephemeral snapshots earlier. That is, we provide enough to repro but not store PII in plain form.

[06:45] Tom Reynolds: What about data residency? Our students are EU-based; we can't have persisted data in US data centers.

[06:55] Lina Ortega: We have region locks. When you create a tenant you can pin region: eu-west-1, eu-central, etc. Request storage, model routing, and logs remain in-region; our control plane lives in multiple regions but we can configure control plane isolation for Private deployments.

[07:20] Priya Singh: About the Optimize piece - we want to reduce tokens and cost but can't degrade model output quality for student answers. How does Redwood Optimize suggest batching or quantization without exposing more PII?

[07:36] Devon Shah: Optimize runs locally on your telemetry and suggests batching profiles and quantization levels. It reports potential delta in quality using your eval test set. Important: suggestions do not require sending raw requests to Redwood; you can run Optimize on masked telemetry or a synthetic eval set. Also, Optimize can recommend prefix caching for repeated prompts (e.g. static system prompts) which saves cost and doesn't risk extra storage because cache keys are hashed.

[08:02] Sara Milton: Does quantization impact hallucination or safety?

[08:08] Devon Shah: It can slightly affect generation quality at very aggressive quantization. Optimize provides an expected ROUGE/EM-like delta based on your eval prompts. You can set thresholds for acceptable degradation. For student-facing content, we'd recommend conservative quant levels and more caching/batching instead.

[08:28] Alex Park: Can we test with a copy of our dataset? We don't want anything leaving our environment — can we run the POC in Private mode?

[08:38] Elena Park: Yes, you can do Private deployment on your VPC or on-prem. For a fast start we usually do a hosted pilot with region set to your EU region and BYOK so NOTHING is readable by Redwood. If you need on-prem for compliance we can scope that but it adds time. Since you said two weeks, hosted with BYOK is the fastest.

[09:05] Tom Reynolds: Walk me through RBAC and SSO. Compliance needs to know who accessed snapshots, who rotated keys etc.

[09:15] Devon Shah: We integrate with SAML SSO providers; you map groups to roles in Console. All access to snapshots, key operations, and policy changes generate audit events and we persist the audit log for the retention window you choose (audit logs are small and can be kept longer under separate legal review). You can also forward audit logs to your SIEM via secure webhook.

[09:44] Jordan Lee: Are audit logs ever stored with full content?

[09:48] Devon Shah: No — audit logs record an event type, actor, resource id, and a redaction diff or token counts. They don't store full request text unless you choose to persist originals.

[10:02] Priya Singh: Ok, show failure/fallback behavior. If your primary model is overloaded or we hit capacity can we fallback to a cached variant without exposing older prompts?

[10:12] Devon Shah: Smart routing can fallback to smaller model variants or allow degraded response that is generated with a reduced context window. Fallback respects route policies: if route is set to ephemeral true, fallbacks won't persist input. If you have a dedicated capacity contract, we can also route to reserved pool.

[10:38] Tom Reynolds: Can we set a policy that anonymizes names in outputs as part of generation and not just redaction?

[10:46] Devon Shah: Yes - we have post-processing hooks where you can apply a transformation pipeline. For example, name->NAME_1 mapping maintained per conversation, or full anonymize where named entities are replaced. That can be enforced at the responder layer.

[11:05] Sara Milton: We're worried about model evaluations – our compliance needs an auditable trail showing a test set passed after any infra change.

[11:12] Lina Ortega: That's in Console under Evals -> Regression Alerts. You can pin eval sets, run pre/post checks for canary rollouts, and get alerts if quality drops beyond a threshold. Each eval run produces an artifact id (we store metrics only unless you choose to persist examples).

[11:36] Priya Singh: Let's talk costs - if we do ephemeral + debug snapshots on demand vs full retention for 30 days, what's the unit economics?

[11:44] Devon Shah: Persisting payloads increases storage and retrieval costs. Rough rule: snapshot-only ephemeral with occasional debug windows reduces request storage spend by ~95% compared to persist 30 days. Main cost factors are token compute, model choice, and optional storage retrieval. We'll send a cost workbook after this call.

[12:05] Tom Reynolds: Competitors like Vertex and Anthropic claim similar privacy controls — how does Redwood differ?

[12:13] Elena Park: Two differentiators: first, unified controls across hosted/dedicated/private with identical API and rollouts. Second, more granular route-level redaction and BYOK for request snapshots so you can do short-term debugging without long-term retention. Plus built-in Optimize that ties directly to cost/quality tradeoffs.

[12:34] Jordan Lee: We need to see a sample policy as code.

[12:38] Devon Shah: Right — here's a policy example in Console policies:
{ "routes": [ {"name":"support-chat","redaction":"pii_strict","storeRequests":false,"debugWindow":"1h","region":"eu-central-1"} ] }
(rough paste, will send full snippet)

[13:10] Alex Park: Will you send a step-by-step onboarding? We want to try enabling ephemeral on a single route and run a few tests.

[13:18] Elena Park: Yes, that's in next steps. Devon will share the runbook and a Postman collection.

[13:25] (short pause, background noise - someone typing)

[13:40] Priya Singh: A couple of compliance clarifications: (1) If we need to produce raw logs for a lawful request, what's the process? (2) How long are the audit logs kept?

[13:52] Devon Shah: (1) We support an eDiscovery workflow: if you choose to keep originals for a retention window under BYOK, you can export them through an admin workflow that requires dual-approval; Redwood does not hold plain-text key material. (2) Audit log retention is configurable; typical customers keep 1-3 years but that has storage and legal implications. Default is 90 days unless extended.

[14:18] Sara Milton: Dual-approval path - is that in Console?

[14:22] Devon Shah: Yes, under Admin -> eDiscovery. You can create a request that requires two authorized approvers; once approved the export package is prepared and encrypted with your KMS and accessible for a limited time.

[14:36] Tom Reynolds: If we do hosted pilot with BYOK, what do you see Redwood having access to?

[14:44] Lina Ortega: With BYOK, Redwood cannot decrypt persisted objects. We hold encrypted blobs and metadata to locate them, but the key is in your KMS. For support we can request signed debug snapshots which you explicitly provide access to for a time-limited window.

[15:00] Jordan Lee: Good. Let's demo a quick flow: set route support-chat to pii_strict + ephemeral, trigger a request with a fake SSN in the message and show redaction.

[15:10] Devon Shah: Ok sending a test message... (typing)
[15:28] Devon Shah: Here's the request payload. (shows console) The redaction pipeline marked SSN-like pattern, replaced with <REDACTED_SSN>. Confidence 0.97. The audit entry shows diff with token counts.

[15:46] Priya Singh: Can an engineer retrieve that diff via API?

[15:50] Devon Shah: Yes — GET /v1/audit/{id} returns metadata and masked diff. Actual originals not returned unless you have export permission and retention set.

[16:05] Tom Reynolds: On debugging, after we get a failing case, what's typical turnaround to get a snapshot?

[16:12] Devon Shah: If debugSnapshot is enabled you get the snapshot immediately; otherwise you can submit a snapshot request which will be captured for the next 1 hour if the trace id shows up. For hosted BYOK there's a signed workflow for us to request a copy only if you accept.

[16:32] Priya Singh: For the POC, we need a performance baseline. We want latency percentiles for RW-large with ephemeral vs persist. Can Redwood run that?

[16:42] Devon Shah: Yes — Devon: we'll run a short benchmark on your dev tenant: 1k requests at typical seq length and report p50/p90/p99. We'll test both storeRequests true and false to compare any I/O impact. Usually storage flag has minimal latency impact except when debugSnapshot is used.

[17:02] Jordan Lee: Any known gotchas with prefix caching and privacy? If we cache part of a prompt that contains user name, will that leak?

[17:12] Devon Shah: Cache keys are hashed and stored separately from identifiable labels. But you should avoid caching full user-provided content; instead cache static system prompts or template expansions. We can also apply a cache sanitizer step to scrub entities before caching.

[17:34] Tom Reynolds: We talked about canary rollouts earlier. If we do A/B with a smaller model for cost savings, who gets what? How do we keep auditability?

[17:44] Lina Ortega: Rollouts are policy-driven, we record rollout id and which requests were routed to variant models. Evals are run on the canary snapshot and we tie each eval result back to the trace id so you can audit.

[18:00] Priya Singh: Ok show me the onboarding page and docs link.

[18:05] Devon Shah: (typing) Link in chat — https://docs.redwood.ai/privacy-controls and the runbook is here: https://redwood-internal.s3/runbooks/willowbrook-poc.zip (we'll share a sanitized public link after call).

[18:22] Alex Park: A note on legal — our counsel will want to see encryption attestations and SOC2.

[18:30] Elena Park: We'll send the SOC2 summary and the encryption whitepaper in the next email.

[18:36] Tom Reynolds: Cool. A couple of micro-questions: 1) If we set redactionProfile to pii_strict, is there a cost for redaction ops? 2) Are redaction confidence scores retained?

[18:48] Devon Shah: (1) Redaction is a small compute op; it's bundled into request processing and not billed separately but small overhead on request latency; we'll quantify in the workbook. (2) Confidence scores for redactions are stored in audit metadata and exported in CSV for your compliance runs.

[19:10] Sara Milton: On the review queue — can compliance have a read-only view of redaction diffs and flagged items?

[19:18] Devon Shah: Yes, RBAC supports a compliance role that can view flagged items and queue details without access to originals.

[19:28] Priya Singh: Let's talk about a failure scenario: keys compromised. What's the revoke path?

[19:36] Devon Shah: You revoke the key in KMS; new objects are encrypted with new key. For historical objects encrypted with old key, you either keep them encrypted (and rotate access via KMS) or request a secure export then re-encrypt with a new key in a controlled workflow. These ops are audited and require RBAC approvals.

[19:58] Jordan Lee: Any SLA around debug snapshot retrieval?

[20:04] Devon Shah: For Dedicated we can include a debug retrieval SLA; for Hosted the normal support SLAs apply. We'll include specifics in the enterprise proposal.

[20:20] (discussion about team roles, off-topic chatter about upcoming holiday)

[24:30] (skip a segment - deep demo, screen scrolling)

[28:02] Devon Shah: I'm now switching to the Optimize tab - here's a recommended profile for your workload: batching window 20ms, dynamic batch size up to 32, prefix cache enabled, quantization q4_0 conservative. The estimate shows 22% cost savings with <0.5% eval delta on your sample.

[28:35] Priya Singh: That looks promising. Can you run Optimize locally on our masked logs?

[28:42] Devon Shah: Yes — we can provide a Docker image for offline run or you can upload masked telemetry; Optimize supports both. We'll coordinate offline run with your infra team.

[29:00] Tom Reynolds: For the POC, can we run Optimize recommendations but force no quantization change and only use caching? We want to isolate effects.

[29:10] Devon Shah: Absolutely — recommendations are modular, you can accept only caching suggestions.

[29:20] Priya Singh: Any regulatory red lines we need to know? For example, student data in US for non-edu research is a no go.

[29:30] Elena Park: If data residency forbids moving data out, hosted with EU region and BYOK is usually acceptable. If law forbids cloud processing at all, then on-prem Private deployment is the only route. We'll help counsel with language.

[29:50] Jordan Lee: A technical nit - do your telemetry collectors strip HTML or attachments?

[29:56] Devon Shah: We provide pre-filters: strip HTML, remove attachments, and run entity redaction. For attachments we don't parse content unless you enable document ingestion pipelines.

[30:12] Sara Milton: If a student pastes their medical info, can we automatically escalate to human review?

[30:18] Devon Shah: Yes — set the review threshold on pii_strict and route flagged items into a compliance review queue. Those flagged items will expose redaction diffs, not originals unless retention chosen.

[30:35] Alex Park: Ok, what's the proposed pilot scope?

[30:40] Elena Park: Proposed pilot: two-week hosted pilot in eu-central with BYOK, enable ephemeral for support-chat with debugSnapshot on for first 48h, run Optimize offline on masked telemetry, run perf baseline and send cost workbook.

[30:55] Priya Singh: Works for me, pending Sara review.

[31:00] Sara Milton: I'll confirm. One more: do you integrate with our ticketing system? We want snapshots attached to tickets.

[31:08] Devon Shah: Yes - we have connectors for Jira and Zendesk to push redaction diffs and snapshot links to tickets. You control which fields are attached.

[31:22] Tom Reynolds: What about retention lifecycles for exports? After we export for legal we need auto-delete policy.

[31:30] Devon Shah: Exports are time-limited and can be set to auto-delete after X days; we also support expiring signed URLs on export packages.

[31:44] (brief side convo about timezones)

[32:10] Priya Singh: Ok - let's confirm who does what.

[32:14] Elena Park: I'll send SOC2 and security pack by Friday. Devon will send runbook and Postman collection. Priya will confirm sample dataset and evaluation metrics; Jordan will coordinate infra onboarding.

[32:30] Tom Reynolds: Fine. Technical question - how do you handle concatenated PII patterns? E.g., name+email in same field?

[32:40] Devon Shah: Redaction profiles run multi-pass. First regex pass, then model-assisted named-entity masking to capture concatenated patterns. Confidence and token offsets are in the audit diff.

[33:00] Sara Milton: Is there any manual tuning required for academic names? We have unusual names and short IDs.

[33:06] Devon Shah: You can provide a allowlist/denylist for custom profile to avoid false positives. Also we can run a short calibration pass on a sample dataset to tune sensitivity.

[33:20] Priya Singh: For the two-week POC we need a checklist for success: 1) no PII persists without BYOK; 2) audit logs capture necessary events; 3) perf delta <= 5% for p90; 4) Optimize shows cost delta > 10% with acceptable quality.

[33:38] Elena Park: We'll add that as acceptance criteria in the pilot doc.

[33:45] Jordan Lee: Devops question: do we need special network egress rules for hosted?

[33:52] Devon Shah: No special egress is required, standard TLS outbound to Redwood endpoints. For Private on VPC we provide a manifest of required ports.

[34:06] Tom Reynolds: About keys again — if we rotate keys on KMS side will it cause a re-encryption job that spikes CPU?

[34:14] Devon Shah: Re-encryption is incremental and can be scheduled during low load. We stream re-encryption jobs and throttle them to avoid spikes.

[34:30] (customer asks about price; Elena gives high-level ranges)

[36:05] Elena Park: Pricing note - the hosted pilot is free; after pilot we provide usage estimate and optional reserved capacity pricing for Dedicated if you want throughput guarantees.

[36:30] Priya Singh: Great. Any security attestations about hardware? We might need HSM-backed keys.

[36:38] Lina Ortega: We can configure HSM keys and provide attestation documentation. We'll include details in the security pack.

[36:48] (short lull)

[37:10] Priya Singh: Let's confirm the timeline: SOC2 docs by 2028-09-09, runbook by 2028-09-10, onboarding for pilot by 2028-09-12, pilot start 2028-09-13, perf baseline complete 2028-09-17, final decision 2028-09-28.

[37:28] Elena Park: Sounds good, we'll aim for that.

[37:32] Tom Reynolds: Are there any limitations around attachments—specifically transcript pdfs containing PII?

[37:40] Devon Shah: You can route attachments through the document ingestion pipeline that supports redaction and then store metadata. If you don't enable ingestion they are not parsed or stored.

[37:55] Sara Milton: For eDiscovery requests, what's the format of exports?

[38:00] Devon Shah: Exports come as an encrypted tarball with JSON lines containing audit metadata, redaction diffs, and optionally original payloads depending on retention choices.

[38:18] Priya Singh: Ok I think we're aligned. Any open risks?

[38:24] Elena Park: The main risk is timeline if you require on-prem deploy; hosted BYOK reduces that risk. Also need to validate calibration of redaction profiles on your data.

[38:36] Tom Reynolds: That is doable. Send the workbook and we'll review.

[38:42] Devon Shah: We'll also include sample scripts to automate redaction profile updates if you have new patterns.

[39:00] (brief side conversation about internals of caching, SE gives a quick overview)

[40:14] Devon Shah: Quick note: for developer ergonomics we have SDK flags to set storeRequests at client level, and route-level overrides so you can centralize policy.

[40:30] Priya Singh: Can we have alerts when a threshold of flagged items per day is breached?

[40:38] Devon Shah: Yes — Console alarms can alert via Slack, PagerDuty, or email.

[40:46] Jordan Lee: Any content moderation tie-ins? If a flagged item indicates abuse do you auto-block generation?

[40:55] Devon Shah: We have optional moderation steps that can block or escalate. They run as part of pipeline pre-checks.

[41:10] Tom Reynolds: One last technical — what's the storage path for ephemeral snapshots? Are they stored in ephemeral storage on nodes or encrypted object store?

[41:22] Devon Shah: Snapshots are written to encrypted object store, but with ephemeral TTL and BYOK. For private on-prem, snapshots can be configured to remain on local block storage and flushed.

[41:38] Priya Singh: All right. Let's close with action items and owners.

[41:44] Elena Park: Action items recap: Elena send SOC2/security pack; Devon send runbook and Postman; Priya confirm dataset; Jordan coordinate onboarding; Redwood to schedule perf baseline week of 9/17.

[42:05] Priya Singh: We'll have a follow-up internal call and then reconvene.

[42:12] Tom Reynolds: Thanks Elena, Devon. Good demo.

[42:18] Elena Park: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and the workbook.

[42:24] (call ends, lingering small talk as people leave)
